decisions.claim: B showed or shared something cute involving a monkey suit and Hello Kitty
decisions.reason: Turn 1 'it's really cute' presupposes B showed/shared something to A; the mention of monkey suit and Hello Kitty indicates the item involves both. Valid E2 presupposition.
decisions.counterexample: B could have shown something involving only one of these elements, but A's phrasing links both to the same item.

decisions.claim: B may have been born in the year of the monkey (A asks this as a question)
decisions.reason: This merely restates that A asked a question. Questions do not establish their answers. The 'may have' hedge makes it a non-attribute meta-observation about A's inquiry rather than a fact about B.
decisions.counterexample: A could ask the question and B could answer 'No, I was born in the year of the tiger.'

decisions.claim: B responded to A's question about being born in the year of the monkey, and A found B's answer explanatory
decisions.reason: This infers B's unseen response content from A's reaction. We cannot know what B said—'Not at all!' could mean B denied the monkey year, or B said something else entirely. Speculating on B's reply is forbidden.
decisions.counterexample: B might have said 'No, I was born in the year of the snake' and A's 'That explains everything' could refer to something else B said.

decisions.claim: B is associated with a monkey suit (wears, owns, or is linked to one)
decisions.reason: Turn 1 'But why a monkey suit?' presupposes B is associated with a monkey suit (wears, owns, or is linked to one). The possessive/question presupposes B's connection to the suit.
decisions.counterexample: The monkey suit could belong to a third party B merely showed, but B is still 'associated' with it in the broad sense.

decisions.claim: B was born in the year of the monkey (Chinese zodiac)
decisions.reason: Turn 3 is a question—questions do not establish answers. Turn 5 'That explains everything' is ambiguous about what B actually confirmed. Treating a question + ambiguous follow-up as presupposing the answer is speculative.
decisions.counterexample: B could have answered 'No, I was born in the year of the pig' and A's 'That explains everything' could refer to something else entirely.

decisions.claim: B likely confirmed being born in the year of the monkey (since A says 'That explains everything' after B's reply to the question)
decisions.reason: This infers B's unseen reply from A's reaction. 'That explains everything' does not confirm B said 'yes'—B could have denied it or given unrelated information. Speculating on B's response content is forbidden.
decisions.counterexample: B might have said 'No, but I love monkeys' and A's 'That explains everything' could refer to the monkey love, not the birth year.
